sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Google successfully booted up its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, which launched into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Using the onboard Gemma 4 model, the satellite generated its first response, a space-themed haiku, alongside telemetry prompts. The spacecraft carries four Tensor Processing Units, though power limits allow only one to operate at a time.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The project explores whether data centres can operate in space to process distributed AI workloads. Orbit exposes hardware to thermal stress and cosmic radiation, which can trigger bit flips in memory and corrupt data. Google aims to test whether inference workloads remain viable under these real-world conditions rather than ground simulations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Google will test how the processors withstand orbital conditions before launching two interconnected satellites in 2027. Those future spacecraft will feature higher power generation and optical links.
